composition.unit_template: Each broad-group frame contains several occupation paths with endpoint circles, a group label, and the net change in that group’s share.
composition.repeat_rule: Repeat ten broad groups horizontally in the published order, with identical y scale and panel widths. Layout uses whitespace deliberately rather than shrinking to each group’s extent.
composition.calculations: Proposed reconstruction: weighted occupation counts divided by all eligible middle-class jobs in that year, times 1,000. This denominator ignores occupation/group filters. Within a repeated group, sum the occupation shares and subtract 1980 from 2012; this follows the chosen occupation set. Gender shares retain their source occupation-year population and ignore display/highlight filters.
composition.guides_annotations_highlights: Sparse horizontal guides preserve comparisons; selected occupations receive anchored callouts. Path endpoint colors interpolate between the two observed gender shares, rather than implying intermediate-year observations.

minimum_data_table: occupation, broad_group, year, weighted_jobs, jobs_per_1000, male_share; two rows per occupation, likely hundreds after aggregation. Exact full-series count is unverified.

source_data.schema: The author provides a companion image with rounded values for 20 growing and 20 shrinking occupations, but no verified complete numeric table or gender-share download.
source_data.license: IPUMS data require registration and compliance with its terms/citation requirements. The NYT graphic remains a credited published reference.
source_data.cleaning: Obtain harmonized 1980 Census/2012 ACS employment, occupation, sex, income and person weights; verify the original eligibility definition, inflation conversion, and occupation crosswalk before claiming replication.
source_data.evidence: Author page and standalone graphic opened; dates/bylines visually checked. IPUMS confirms harmonized Census/ACS availability. NYT interactive access was unavailable, so exact underlying data are not labeled Available.

difficulty_reason: Composition is tractable after aggregation, but matching the original population and taxonomy requires research. Gradient strokes and numeric endpoint circles exceed M2 paths alone.

verification.image: Author-hosted standalone online graphic, not the full newspaper spread; visually inspected
verification.data_checks: Companion rounded 40-occupation table inspected; full microdata-to-graphic schema not recovered

title: More days at the highest temperatures in 2023
creator_publisher: Erwan Rivault, BBC News; article by Mark Poynting and Erwan Rivault, January 9, 2024. The creator's Information is Beautiful Awards submission verifies the graphic credit.
what_it_shows: Daily global temperature anomalies form one distribution for every year from 1940 through 2023. The ridge positions move toward the warm side of a fixed historical baseline, while annotations distinguish the exceptional 2023 distribution from earlier record years.
why_it_fits: One simple repeated silhouette supports a full editorial composition: shared scales, selected annotations, gradient color, and an explanatory miniature. The static image carries the argument without interaction.

composition.artboard: 1280 × 2530 pixels, approximately 1:2, white; main chart above a short how-to-read footer.
composition.text_elements: Headline, baseline definition, selected year labels, temperature ticks at top and bottom, three year callouts, reading instructions and source credit. The footer explains height as the frequency of days.
composition.scales: A shared horizontal temperature-anomaly scale uses the 1991–2020 daily baseline. One common vertical density/count multiplier is added to each year’s fixed baseline. Color varies continuously with anomaly from cooler to warmer values; years keep fixed positions from 1940 at the top to 2023 at the bottom.
composition.unit_template: One XY frame draws 84 translated lower/upper band series and their ordered outlines. Gradient fill is keyed to the shared anomaly x coordinate. Inter-band occlusion happens inside this frame, so no overlapping-repeat-frame capability is needed.
composition.repeat_rule: None; one band series per year within a single frame, drawn in a fixed order. Year labels and selected callouts are fixed annotations. The small how-to-read example is an independently authored, one-time explanatory element.
composition.calculations: For each year, anomaly distributions use that year’s daily observations against the fixed 1991–2020 reference. The available recreation supplies 25 bins with a 365-count total per year; the original BBC smoothing kernel is unverified. Upstream density preparation must state its bandwidth and treatment of those bins. Year visibility filters preserve baselines, shared height scale, and draw order; observation filters require recomputation upstream. Never rebase anomalies to the visible years.
composition.guides_annotations_highlights: Zero is a shared reference; selected 1998, 2016, and 2023 labels attach to their fixed year baselines and curves within the shared frame. The instructional mini-ridge and its labels are a separately authored one-time explanation, not a second frame inside every repeat.

minimum_data_table: year, anomaly_x, density_or_bin_count, baseline_y, lower_y, upper_y, draw_order; the checked reconstruction has 84 × 25 = 2,100 year-bin records. Convert bins to declared density curves upstream; fixed baseline offsets place all bands in one frame.
source_data: The open recreation's CSV body was downloaded: its first column is Temperature difference from 1991-2020 avg (°C), followed by year columns 1940 through 2023. Its source template documents daily ERA5 temperatures, subtraction of the 1991–2020 daily reference, and 0.1°C bins. Unpivot those columns; do not mistake the counts for daily records. This supplies a defensible reconstruction, but the original BBC density bandwidth is unverified. No dataset-specific license was found on the inspected recreation page or CSV; retain C3S/ECMWF attribution.
difficulty_reason: Eighty-four overlapping gradients need stable draw order, legible year callouts, and honest upstream smoothing.

verification.checks_and_limits: Static BBC image visually inspected; no animation dependency. Web reader blocked BBC, but direct HTML retrieval succeeded. Binned reconstruction is available; exact original kernel/rounding is not.

capability_notes: M2/M3 can draw translated band coordinates in one frame. The remaining geometric styling gap is continuous fill color across an area; density estimation is explicitly upstream.
